To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the QGP is a quantum liquid-like system with a strong tendency to form glueballs, and that it is rather viscous.
the QGP is a strongly interacting quantum liquid at all temperatures, and the shear viscosity-to-entropy density ratio is in the range $1/4 \pi < \eta / S < 2.1/4 \Pi$.

the QGP is a quantum liquid-like state, that the QGP viscosity is of the same order as the one of a weakly interacting gas of quarks and gluons and that the heavy-quark self-diffusion in the QGP is appreciably larger than the one in a weakly interacting plasma.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: 1) the structure of the QCD phase diagram at finite temperature and density, 2) transport properties of the quark gluon plasma and 3) the equation of state of the quark matter at high baryon densities.
the development of the PIMC and Wigner dynamics methods for the QGP and their application for calculation of the thermodynamic and transport properties of the quark plasma.
a new approach to the study of the quark- gluon plasma based on the path-integral methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while the QGP is a strongly interacting system, the interactions are not so strong as to make the system behave like a perfect liquid.

the QGP behaves like a quantum liquid with a high degree of correlation between its constituent degrees of freedom and that its viscosity-to-entropy density ratio, $\eta/S$, is in the range of values expected for a liquid.
the PIMCs are a promising tool for investigation of the thermodynamics and transport properties of the strongly interacting quark-gluons system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the color path-integral PIMC method, when applied to the QGP, is a promising tool for the investigation of thermodynamic and transport properties of this strongly interacting quantum liquid.
the QGP, at least up to 440 Me V, is a strongly coupled quantum liquid with a large shear viscosity and a small heavy-quark diffusion coefficient, and with a large heavy-quark diffusion.
the PIMCS and Wigner dynamics methods are able to reproduce the thermodynamic and transport properties of the hot and dense QGP in a satisfactory manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of a quantum path-integral method for calculation of the thermodynamics and Wigner dynamics for calculation of the transport properties is an efficient approach for investigation of strongly interacting matter at high temperature and/or density.

the PIMP method is able to yield reliable results on the thermodynamic and transport properties of the strongly-interacting matter at temperatures above the phase transition and can be used to study the properties of the quark-hadron mixed phase.
the QGP at temperatures above the transition point is a quantum liquid rather than a classical gas.
